injuries.description: significant disability in his right lower limb with residual pain in the affected areas for the rest of his life
source: It is accepted that the plaintiff has been left with a significant disability in his right lower limb and will have residual pain in the affected areas for the rest of his life.

The plaintiff was also diagnosed with adjustment disorder and PTSD, suffering from depression, anxiety, low mood irritability, insomnia, frequent flashbacks and nightmares. He is still on anti depressant medication. Although his mental health has improved, further psychiatric treatment and medication is required.

manifestations.description: residual pain in the affected areas for the rest of his life
depression, anxiety, low mood, irritability, insomnia, frequent flashbacks and nightmares
persistent right ankle, knee and hip joint pain
pain in his right distal leg and proximal tibia if he stood for over 10 minutes or walked three to four steps
could walk for only half an hour before he required a break
significant stiffness of the right ankle joint
degenerative osteoarthritis of the ankle (persistent ankle pain showing degenerative osteoarthritis)
significant depression in 2013 requiring ongoing psychiatric help

treatments_received: four surgical operations including the placement of nails, pins and screws to repair the extensive damage to his right leg
removal of implants up to May 2014 (surgeries on 5 March and 18 June 2012 and further removals up to May 2014)
physiotherapy (first course between 28 October 2010 and 1 February 2012; further courses noted in 2012 and ongoing)
occupational therapy (first received on 28 September 2011; further OT in June 2012)
clinical psychology sessions (6 times from August 2012 to June 2013)
medication including pregabalin, propranalol, fluoxine, trazodone and lorazepam
treatments_future: debridement surgery to relieve degenerative osteoarthritis of the ankle scheduled for November 2015
further corrective surgery (ongoing five years after the Accident) with further surgery scheduled November 2015

losses.description: Significant disability in his right lower limb with residual pain in the affected areas for the rest of his life.
Reduced standing and walking tolerance: standing tolerance of 10 minutes; pain after walking three to four steps; could walk for only half an hour before requiring a break.
Ongoing psychiatric symptoms including depression, anxiety, low mood, irritability, insomnia, frequent flashbacks and nightmares requiring ongoing psychiatric treatment and medication.
